question.text:
Consider the following basic block:

$$
\begin{aligned}
& w=x+y \\
& z=w * 2 \\
& x=y+z \\
& w=x-y
\end{aligned}
$$


The minimum number of NODES and the total number of OPERATOR LABELS required to represent the operations in the DAG of the above basic block, respectively, are:

  1. $7$ and $3$
     
  2. $9$ and $7$
     
  3. $6$ and $3$
     
  4. $8$ and $4$
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
Consider the following basic block:

$$
\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{t} 1=\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b} \\
& \mathrm{t} 2=\mathrm{c}+\mathrm{d} \\
& \mathrm{t} 3=\mathrm{t} 1 * 2 \\
& \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{t} 2-\mathrm{a} \\
& \mathrm{t} 4=\mathrm{t} 3 / \mathrm{a}
\end{aligned}
$$


The minimum number of NODES and minimum DIRECTED EDGES present in the DAG representation of the above basic block, respectively, are:

  1. $9$ and $12$
     
  2. $7$ and $9$
     
  3. $10$ and $13$
     
  4. $10$ and $10$
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
A lexical analyzer uses the following regular expressions (REs) to recognize four tokens, $T_1, T_2$, $T_3$, and $T_4$, over the alphabet $\Sigma=\{a, b, c\}$.

  • $T_1:(a \mid b)^* a$
     
  • $T_2:(a \mid b)^* b$
     
  • $T_3: c(a|b| c)^*$
     
  • $T_4:(a|b| c) c$
     

The analyzer follows two standard rules:

  1. Longest Possible Prefix Match: The longest matching prefix is selected.
     
  2. Precedence: If two or more tokens match the same longest prefix, the token rule specified earliest takes precedence ( $T_1>T_2>T_3>T_4$ ).
     

If the analyzer is processing the input string:
$$\textbf{bbacabc}$$
What is the complete sequence of tokens generated by the lexical analyzer?

  1. $T_2, T_1, T_3$
     
  2. $T_1,T_3,T_4$
     
  3. $T_1,T_3$
     
  4. $T_1,T_3,T_4$
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
Consider the following canonical set of LR(0) items:

$$
I_5=\left\{\begin{array}{l}
R \rightarrow x \cdot P y \\
R \rightarrow x P \\
P \rightarrow y
\end{array}\right.
$$


Which of the following describes the set of conflicts (if any) present in State $I_5$ ?

  1. A shift-reduce conflict on the symbol $P$ and a reduce-reduce conflict on the symbol $y$. 
     
  2. A shift-reduce conflict on the symbol $P$ but no reduce-reduce conflict. 
     
  3. A reduce-reduce conflict only. 
     
  4. A shift-reduce conflict on the symbol $y$ and a reduce-reduce conflict on the symbol $\$$ (end-of-input).
question.subject: Compiler Design

question.text:
Consider the following C code snippet:

float val = 2.0;
/* Check Condition */
if (val <= MAX) {
    val /= 2;
}


What is the total number of tokens identified by the lexical analyzer for the given code snippet (ignoring whitespace)?
